text:
maria: quick sync — we need to decide how SM-level metrics (occupancy, slot_memory_bytes, queue_depth) get surfaced for both hosted + dedicated pools. two decisions: 1) telemetry keys (what we tag by) 2) which keys are used as quota/routing inputs.

jon: +1. do we have a proposed schema? can we avoid exploding cardinality by tagging too many things? :eyes:

maria: thinking minimal set: pool_type (hosted|dedicated), pool_id, sm_id, model_family, region, customer_tier. use model_variant only for sampling/rolling up, not per-request.

ashley: from oncall POV we need sm_health and queue_depth per pool_id and region at 30s granularity. detailed per-sm only for traces/canaries. otherwise alerts will be noisy.

kevin: console ask — product wants two new dashboard panes: (A) per-pool occupancy heatmap (by sm_id collapsed to host rows) (B) per-customer headroom view (aggregate across dedicated pools). Can we expose a single metric that feeds both without double-counting?

maria: yes — emit occupancy_percent (0-100) and slot_memory_bytes. downstream rollups: mean and p95 over window. headroom = capacity - sum(current_allocated). prefer derived in the console, not in telemetry producer.

runtime-bot: telemetry proto suggestion:
```
message SmMetrics {
  string pool_type = 1; // hosted|dedicated
  string pool_id = 2;
  string sm_id = 3;
  string region = 4;
  string model_family = 5;
  double occupancy_percent = 6;
  uint64 slot_memory_bytes = 7;
  uint32 queue_depth = 8;
  uint64 timestamp_ms = 9;
}
```

jon: if we keep pool_id + region + model_family that should limit cardinality. do we plan to tag by customer_id for dedicated? that could blow up.

maria: for dedicated, we need customer_tag for headroom per-customer. but keep that optional and sampled. default ingest is customer-agnostic aggregate; separate hop for customer-level telemetry (enabled by reserved pools only).

ashley: alert rules proposal:
- pool occupancy p95 > 85% for 5m -> page
- queue_depth avg > 50 for 3m -> page
- slot_memory_bytes delta spike -> warn channel

kevin: UX note — in console we want a toggle: "Show per-customer" which hits a different API that returns aggregates keyed by customer_id. need APi surfaces: /metrics/pool/{pool_id}/heatmap and /metrics/pool/{pool_id}/headroom?customer=true

maria: routing/quota question: should routing decisions use occupancy_percent directly, or use a derived backpressure_signal (0..1) exposed by allocator?

jon: prefer derived backpressure_signal. keeps routing code simpler and we can change mapping without re-instrumenting. also easier to blackbox for hosted tiers.

maria: agreed. runtime will emit backpressure_signal (float) plus occupancy. routing policy will consume backpressure_signal and fallback thresholds per customer_tier.

runtime-bot: sample event with routing fields:
```
{
  "pool_id":"gpu-hosted-a",
  "backpressure_signal":0.73,
  "occupancy_percent":78.5,
  "quanta_window_s":30
}
```

kevin: one more ask — add model_family label so console can split heatmaps by LLM family. not required for routing.

maria: will file PR with telemetry proto + ingestion contract and add a small canary pipeline to emit into metrics.gpu.sm for one hosted pool. tagging plan: pool_type,pool_id,region,model_family,optional customer_id.

jon: please include ingestion cost estimate (cardinality * qps) in PR. finance needs a heads up for prometheus/sink costs.

maria: noted — I’ll include a quick calc. plan: canary for 48h, then ramp to other hosted pools, then expose dedicated optional path.

ashley: oncall: add runbook note for "high queue depth" -> look at recent deploys, check allocator fallbacks, notify infra.

kevin: I’ll sketch console wireframes after PR lands.

maria: thanks all — action items: maria open PR with proto + cardinality calc, runtime add backpressure_signal impl, console owners (kevin) wireframes, oncall (ashley) update runbook. ping here when PR is up. :thumbsup:
